events.text: Volvo acquired Carrus; its models then sold in Europe under other names.

evidence.quote: After Carrus was acquired by Volvo in 1998

events.text: 9700 range introduced as replacement for Carrus Star and Vector/Regal models.

evidence.quote: It was introduced in 2001 as a replacement for the Carrus Star and Vector/Regal models

events.text: Volvo unified all earlier models under the single name Volvo 9700.

evidence.quote: In 2001 Volvo gathered all the different models to one name , Volvo 9700

events.text: 9700HD serial production started, summer 2001.

evidence.quote: Serial production of 9700H and
9700HD started in the summer of 2001

events.text: 9700S came into production, autumn 2001.

evidence.quote: 9700HD started in the summer of 2001 , while 9700S came into production in the autumn

events.text: Body model also offered on Carrus Star 503/603 chassis in Nordic countries.

evidence.quote: In 2001 and 2002 , the body model was also available on other chassises

events.text: Volvo Polska plant in Wroclaw started production of 9700H and 9700HD.

evidence.quote: In 2003 production also started at Volvo Polska Sp . z o.o . in Wrocław , Poland

events.text: Small batch of 9700S built on B7R chassis for a Finnish operator.

evidence.quote: a small batch of 9700S were built on B7R chassis in 2004 for a Finnish operator

events.text: Model received a minor facelift.

evidence.quote: In 2004 the model received a minor facelift

events.text: Finnish plants renamed: Tampere and Turku factories.

evidence.quote: That year the Finnish plants were renamed

events.text: 9700 NG (New Generation) revealed.

evidence.quote: The Volvo 9700 NG , also known as 9700 New/Next Generation was revealed in the autumn of 2006

events.label: award
events.text: 9700 NG awarded Coach of the Year 2008 by European bus journalists.

evidence.quote: In 2007 , the 9700 NG was awarded the title Coach of the Year 2008

events.text: Volvo closed its operations in Finland, including the Tampere plant.

evidence.quote: On 1 October 2008 , Volvo closed their operations in Finland

events.text: Lieto plant sold back to Finnish investors, mostly Carrus-related.

evidence.quote: The Tampere plant closed and the Lieto plant was sold back to Finnish investors

events.text: Lieto plant's new name became Carrus Delta Oy.

evidence.quote: On 1 October 2008 , Volvo closed their operations in Finland
The new name became Carrus Delta Oy

events.text: Higher-power engines moved from B12B to B13R chassis after Euro V.

evidence.quote: until late 2009 when Euro V emission requirements were enforced

events.text: 9700 available in North America via Prevost network, 45 tri-axle coach.

evidence.quote: the Volvo 9700 has been available as a 45 ( 13.7 m ) tri-axle coach in North America since 2009

events.text: 9700S restriction to B12B/B9R chassis ended with B11R introduction.

evidence.quote: B11R in 2011 , the 9700S could only be delivered with 340 hp ( B12B ) or 380 hp ( B9R )

events.text: 9700 UG (Upgrade) first revealed for Nordic markets.

evidence.quote: The Volvo 9700 UG , also known as 9700 Upgrade , was first revealed in November 2012

events.text: Finnish production switched entirely to the UG version.

evidence.quote: the production at the plant in Finland was all changed to UG by early 2013

events.text: Third generation 9700 Grand presented, designed for Mexico.

evidence.quote: Third generation was presented in 2013 , known as 9700 Grand

events.text: Fourth generation 9700 unveiled.

evidence.quote: The fourth generation 9700 was unveiled in May 2018

events.text: Double-decker 9700DD launched on Volvo B11RLE chassis.

evidence.quote: A double decker version of the fourth generation 9700 , the 9700DD , was launched in February 2020

events.text: Lower 4 m-height 9700DD version launched.

evidence.quote: a lower , 4 m-height version was launched a year later

undated_mentions: Rollout of the UG generation to the rest of Europe postponed to the autumn Euro VI chassis introduction (year not stated)
